身怀绝技的猎人加上风格迥异的战车，带大家重回少年时。 战斗随机性较强，操作简单。 以后会有徒步作战吗？毕竟……战车怎可与血肉之躯匹敌！

内容有点太少，但看在重装机兵得份上，还是先给好评吧。 一些建议： 1.如果可以，武器得LV3效果尽量更有趣，虽然我知道你的设计思路是土豆兄弟不是幸存者，但因为内容量的关系，BD现得非常蛋疼，几乎没有太多可以操作得空间（缺乏土豆兄弟里的种类繁多的无限叠加的属性道具），单靠武器BD玩了两局之后非常无聊，几乎每次都是一样的效果。 2.角色系统因为缺乏花样现得毫无意义，同样的，战车系统因为抠抠搜搜的给，玩起来也几乎没有太大差异（尤其是主炮/副炮/SE，几乎定死了可以玩的BD，这一点土豆兄弟里非常自由，所以不是一个好的参考，感觉可以随时花钱修改洞更好一些）很难从现有的设计中体验到想要的那种类似【六主炮神教】的快感，在战车的限制上实在是太多了。 总之，怎么玩都感觉不舒服，不畅快，既没有幸存者的爽感，也没有土豆兄弟的构筑目标，建议想清楚自己想要的最终方向效果。

Came for the pixel art, stayed for the roguelike builds. 8 hours in and I'm still experimenting with different tank setups and weapon synergies. Fast combat, satisfying builds, and bosses that actually make you think. Just beat the first Hunting Mode boss. Already planning the next run. Easy recommendation if you like roguelikes.

Simple, but with enought depth to keep me entertained. Mixing and upgrading your gear through a run and trying different builds. The unlocks und meta upgrades are well balanced. (at least for my taste) + you can save the game and continue (in a way like Brotato) + 5€ in the EU thats very nice

拥有类幸存者的玩法基因，并融合了《赤色要塞》的经典坦克战斗，构建出独特的后末日生存战斗体验。这就是本作，一款后末日废土中背景下的坦克题材弹幕肉鸽游戏，游戏更倾向于《土豆兄弟》那样的玩法和体验，但是缺乏明确的构筑和爽感，可能后续还需要再优化一下。 游戏开场即展现核战后的荒芜世界，锈蚀的广告牌在沙尘暴中摇晃，变异生物在废弃工厂游荡，而玩家扮演的"钢铁猎人"需驾驶改装坦克，在动态生成的地图中完成通缉令任务。游戏采用了一种复古8-bit像素风格，这种将80年代街机美学与现代肉鸽机制结合的设计，让老玩家瞬间找回上世纪游戏黄金时代的热血，又因随机装备组合系统获得新鲜感。 游戏拥有一定的剧情内容，玩家可以通过战斗与探索以及物品寻回来触发一系列剧情，甚至可以通过隐藏内容触发一些隐藏的结局。游戏本来共有9关，但是后面大量的内容都是隐藏的需要一定的探索解锁。 游戏提供超过50种武器模块，从经典链式机枪到实验性电磁轨道炮，每种武器都带有独特属性链，武器之间的组合还可触发各种不同的组合效果，对敌人造成更高的伤害。这也使得游戏拥有一定的深度策略性，甚至有机会得到快速击杀窗口。此外还有驾驶员、车辆、装备构成的战术三角，驾驶证人物能够帮助维修无人机群，恢复装甲等，也可以通过退技能能提升队友伤害等。 总体来说，游戏的可玩性还是非常高的，复古风格的画面与玩法很吸引人，但是目前缺乏快速获取的爽感，到后面密集的弹幕也有点伤眼睛，感觉画面有些乱，可能在后面的更新中还需要再优化一下。

玩法类《土豆兄弟》，特色是多战车操控机制，玩家可以同时操控至多三辆战车，在末日废土中对战通缉犯。 地图活动空间开阔，对走位的要求不算严苛，整体难度相对友好。但因为于配置了引擎跟装备的战车都会受到碰撞跟弹幕伤害，所以操控三辆车的时候躲避起来没有单辆车灵活，刚开始需要适应一下。这里告诉一个小技巧，就是原地转圈，能最大程度减少碰撞体积。 游戏玩起来还是挺爽的，尤其是三辆战车LV3全副武装后，结合带感的音乐，看着满屏的特效击杀就很解压。 游戏看似只有三关，实际上通关后解锁的狩猎模式，还有6个BOSS可挑战，相当于6个关卡。
难度曲线不合理， 后期养成难度较高
简单难度没难度，狩猎难度纯恶心。
普通模式平平无奇，狩猎模式就是纯纯的恶心人了，各种DEBUFF就为了让你不爽，只能用特定组合玩法，说是让玩家尝试多样的组合乐趣但是又用极其恶心的DEBUFF限制你只能玩特定玩法，极其无趣。 以及其他限制太死太多的设定，游玩过程没有一丝快乐。如果你想来爽，那么请换一款游戏。
成长难度过高，羁绊，装备，驾驶员，坦克非常少，刷装备非常难，不建议买
不好玩，没特色，坐牢体验，半成品

设计幽默，装备平衡烂到家，各种设计纯为了恶心玩家。更别说驾驶员甚至还有负面数值。 狩猎模式，负面甚至是全程累积，算上驾驶员的负面你甚至开局就能掉30%的命中，而且没有弥补的可能。并且一把狩猎的收益甚至不如简单难度3（狩猎一把假如你能顺利毕业900，简单3，1000打底）。 闪避有上限，导致烟雾弹这种装备就纯摆设。 词条会掉命中，导致一些“死亡一指”的武器也是各种摆设。 再提一下那个幽默的副炮飞弹，主炮装填的时候才会发射，然而弹药少的主炮根本用不了，弹药多的主炮这东西纯摆设。最常搭配的白色爆裂炮满改奖励还是弹药上限+10。 副炮只有2个选择，一个是金币副炮，一个护盾副炮，顶多配装再加个霰弹。其他的纯废物。 插件也几乎都是尴尬玩意儿。搭配主炮，就一个太阳镜片，算上飞轮连携搭配电极也就两个选择。 发动机，几乎没选择，只有金币箱一个，你玩爆破撑死装一个紫色窜天猴。 主炮不用爆破的基本上只有飞轮一个选择，其他东西属于幽默中的幽默。看上去伤害很高实际上打起来纯幽默。你需要面对四面八方糊过来的敌人，单体根本不能解决问题，群攻、持续性好、入手简单的只有爆破和飞轮2个白装。等于你设计那么多高级武器都是摆设。没任何想用的兴趣。 更别说最高稀有的黄色了。黄色武器只有主炮，而且几乎只有最后两关才可能刷出。搭配红车每关商店必出装备中的东西出率都感人，撑死了也就2个，出1个2星算你非常欧了，你想想有些炮车你是2个主炮槽。再想想看你要9个（1000块）左右才能看到一个完全体，更别说刷新的钱和其他东西。 各种被动芯片也属实抽象，同样因为有上限，闪避类被动基本没意义。暴击几乎涵盖了所有你需要的优势收益，堪称逆天（护盾、装填、追伤）。 作为小品大概只值15块左右，更别说你这个美术素材蹭的重装机兵，机制蹭的幸存者类型，完全没有多少自己的东西。

这款幸存者 like 游戏整体玩法还算不错，装备搭配的自由度很高，玩法深度足够。但目前的问题也比较明显：并不是所有装备都有对应的组合效果，流派搭配和数值平衡还有优化空间。 难度设计上问题比较突出，简单和困难难度差距过于悬殊，阶梯感很生硬，很容易让玩家失去持续刷怪养成的动力。 美术风格有点复古，让人联想到小时候玩的坦克游戏。能理解小工作室资源有限，但世界观和画风的违和感比较强—— 玩家操控坦克，对抗的却是蜗牛、小蜜蜂这类生物，题材和视觉风格割裂感明显，代入感稍弱。
局外成长极为不合理，花了大价钱改造车，结果局内连续刷几次没改造过的坦克，这局直接完蛋。建议局内选坦克的时候能一次多给几个选择，而不是每次只能选一个

I like it. Not a long game but it does things a little differently to other survivors games and its fun. Would benefit from way more map variety and music. Maybe make the tanks harder to unlock and upgrade. I feel like I would have played longer if there was still more to unlock and do.

Very cute little bullet-heaven. It feels spiritually somewhat like a Flash game, but more polished. It's not particularly long or overcomplicated, and somewhat clunky and restricting in how you can build out a tank, but dealing with that and the inventory is also just...one of the mechanics. The controlling is tight, the hit-boxes are fair, the explosions are satisfying, the runs aren't very long. And it's cheap. If you like bullet-heavens(like I do), then you definitely should give it a try.

I didn't expect to lose an hour to this. You know that moment in Brotato when a build finally comes together and everything on screen just melts? BROTANK has that — but you're not doing it with one character. You've got a convoy of tanks, each one independently loaded, and when they all fire at once it's a completely different feeling. My setup: one tank running full bombardment, one napalm and fire, one pure laser. When that combination hit a wave cleanly — explosions layering over burning ground over laser beams — I just sat there for a second. That doesn't happen often with a game in this price range. It's polished in the ways that matter. The weapons are there, the enemies are there, the loop works. If you've played Vampire Survivors or Brotato you'll feel at home in about two minutes. The UI needs work — some mechanics aren't explained well enough and you'll be guessing at a few things early on. The localization has rough edges too. Neither stopped me from having a good time, but they're worth knowing going in. Under $5. Made by a team of 3. If youenjoy Brotato-style games at all, just buy it.
Its a fun time passed. No real in-depth thinking involved. Just strategy on how to avoid death, collect gold, buy upgrades.

玩起来还是有意思的，目前只玩了新手关卡的内容还没玩到狩猎关卡。玩的时候感觉里面的小怪有点疯狗了，比如新手第四关的高速蚂蚁和第五关的乌龟。然后第五关的boss沙漠之虎马拉松+连续激光（这个我觉得转阶段的时候放一次就差不多了）拖时间有点难评，本身boss血量也不低，然后还得躲其他小怪冲脸，很容易就拉开距离了（但是这boss进攻感觉还不如之前的几个），之前有一次打到倒计时结束锁一丝血有点红温。另外第五关的压场火车进场前可以给个区域提示。
每一把时间都不长，正好适合偶尔休闲一把。
Vampire Survivor meets Brotato for under 10$? Can't go wrong!
这个游戏还是有点搭配深度的，必须注意激活连携装备，每种装备的效果几乎都不一样。 个人玩下来觉得游戏有两个地方的手感需要提高： 1、三个坦克连起来的面积太大了，后面两个坦克很容易被打死，感觉要不就是提高后面坦克的免伤，要不就是和其他幸存者一样搞成圆形。 2、人物升级的加点没有特质，没有啥变强的感觉，还不如搞爽点，都变成被动技能可能更有意思一些。

装备系统用的自走棋的合星系统，垃圾，刚开始出紫色金色装备，关卡结束了，逼得你要带经济流的装备。坦克么也不生存，局内没什么升级的选项，不够rouge，各种流派和类别的武器装备之间联动性较弱，或者说基本就是附加一个效果，没有什么质变和大飞跃提升。最rouge的反而是每局局内遇到的随机坦克（虽然一共就那么几种，如果不升级到满还基本上没太大差别）和随机驾驶员。半成品，目前来看都不值这个价钱，大概也就是个十五块钱的品质。

BROTANK is a roguelike action game that takes the familiar concept of surviving endless enemy waves and gives it a refreshing twist through tank-based combat and squad management. Developed and published by Dfirend Games, the title embraces a retro-inspired visual style while combining bullet-hell gameplay, progression systems, and strategic customization. The result is a game that feels immediately accessible yet gradually reveals layers of complexity as players experiment with different builds and tactics. Set in a harsh post-apocalyptic world, players step into the role of a bounty hunter assembling a powerful armored team to survive increasingly dangerous battles. Unlike many roguelikes that focus on controlling a single character, BROTANK allows players to build a squad of tanks and pilots, creating opportunities for unique combinations and specialized roles. This feature gives the game a stronger strategic identity than many of its genre counterparts, encouraging players to think beyond simple damage output and consider how different units can support one another. Combat is fast, energetic, and often chaotic. Swarms of enemies flood the battlefield while projectiles fill the screen, demanding constant movement and quick decision-making. Despite the intensity, the controls remain straightforward, making it easy to jump into the action. Success comes from balancing offense, positioning, and resource management rather than relying purely on reflexes. As enemy numbers increase and stronger opponents emerge, each battle becomes a test of both mechanical skill and build efficiency. A major strength of the game lies in its extensive customization options. Players gain access to a large arsenal of weapons, upgrades, and equipment pieces that can dramatically alter how a run unfolds. Some setups focus on overwhelming firepower, while others emphasize survivability, support capabilities, or specialized synergies. Discovering powerful combinations becomes one of the most satisfying aspects of the experience, and the game constantly rewards experimentation. No two runs feel exactly alike because the available equipment and upgrade choices can push players toward entirely different strategies. The progression system also contributes significantly to the game's replay value. Even unsuccessful attempts provide rewards that can be used to strengthen future runs, creating a steady sense of advancement. Unlockable upgrades, hidden abilities, and new customization opportunities ensure that players are consistently working toward long-term goals. This structure helps soften the frustration that often accompanies difficult roguelikes while maintaining a satisfying challenge. Boss encounters serve as memorable highlights throughout each playthrough. These larger battles require players to adapt to unique attack patterns and identify effective ways to exploit enemy weaknesses. Rather than simply surviving waves of weaker opponents, players must prove that their chosen build can handle major threats under pressure. The bosses provide welcome variety and help punctuate the pacing of each run. Visually, BROTANK embraces classic pixel-art aesthetics that evoke the spirit of older arcade and console games. The retro presentation complements the fast-paced gameplay well, keeping the battlefield readable even during moments of intense action. While the graphics are intentionally simple, they possess a certain charm that fits the game's post-apocalyptic setting and old-school influences. The soundtrack and overall atmosphere further reinforce the feeling of embarking on a dangerous wasteland adventure. The game is not entirely free of drawbacks. Players seeking a deep narrative experience may find the story elements relatively limited, as the primary focus remains on gameplay and progression. Additionally, the sheer number of upgrade options and equipment interactions can initially feel overwhelming. However, those willing to invest time into understanding the systems will likely discover that this depth is one of the game's greatest strengths. Overall, BROTANK succeeds as an entertaining blend of roguelike progression, bullet-hell action, and strategic squad building. Its unique focus on managing multiple tanks, combined with meaningful customization and rewarding progression, helps it stand out in a crowded genre. While it leans more heavily on gameplay depth than storytelling, it delivers a satisfying and highly replayable experience that will appeal to fans of action-heavy roguelikes and build-focused games. Rating: 8/10

The game is trying to present oldschool 8-bit arcade bullet-hell with new elements but after 10 hours it goes repetative and unsatisfying, plus total gacha-upgrades in the bay after wave adds more boredom. Tanks are not bad but drivers and their skills are not so - later stages of run just show that +5 to all stats is better then some skill+ which may do not only good things. So if you new one to genre you may buy it - price is adequite, but for experienced gamers - definitly not. Ukrainian. Гра намагається показати старий стиль 8-бітної аркади у суміші з пекельною стріляниною але після 10 годин гра просто набридає постіними повтореннями, до того ж гача (лотерея) у ангарі після щойної хвилі дуже дратує. Танки непогані, але водії не такі вже корисні особливо їх навички - на пізньому етапі забігу отримати +5 до характеристик набагато краще ніж навичку+ яка ще й може нашкодити. Тож якщо ви новенький то можете придбати - ціна невисока, але якщо досвідчений - цілковито точно ні. Russian. Игра старается показать смесь старой 8-битной аркады с пулеадом, но после 10 часов становится слишком повторяющейся, а ещё эти гача (лотерейные) апгрейды после волн крайне раздражают. Танки неплохи, но вот водители уже не так особенно их навыки - на позднем этапе забега получить +5 к характеристикам намного лучше чем навык+ который ещё может и навредить. Так что если вы новичок в жанре можете покупать - цена невысокая, но если опытный - совершенно точно нет.

The variety of enemy patterns in Brotank keeps each run feeling unique. You’ll rarely see the same wave twice, which is a big plus for long-term engagement.
Brotank’s content feels substantial for a compact roguelite: tons of weapons, craftable upgrades, and hidden branches that reward exploration.
You’re constantly choosing which upgrades to chase, which pilots to field, and how to adapt to tougher waves of enemies. It’s got the depth you want without overwhelming you.
Mixing weapons and gear to build your own tank squad is the real highlight. Runs stay fast and addictive, and experimenting with different loadouts makes each attempt feel fresh.
Runs feel engaging, mixing survivor-style chaos with tank combat, clever weapon combos. Unlocks and hidden stages keep things interesting, and the retro pixel vibe makes it easy to sink hours in.
The control responsiveness in Brotank is excellent, with precise aiming and smooth movement. It’s the kind of game you feel committed to mastering after a few minutes of play.
USteppin thinks this game is worth your time.
